First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\frac{{sec}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }=\frac{{sec}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }
$$

We now simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{sec}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the following identities: 

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },\,\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta },
$$

 

Using the above identities, we can further simplify our expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{sec}^{3}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .
$$
